sessions.intent: Implement module-owns-action core (element-typed action.Module, ActionName->Name, Create chain, reader contract), then the Validate trilogy on top.

before.assumptions: Architect released module-owns-action as prerequisite for the Validate trilogy (Q1); Q2 settled the split - changes stay builder, verdicts move to nodes. Wire key already 'name'; item base does not claim Name.
before.risk: Large mechanical sweep (~76 prod + ~214 test ActionName sites, 123 test Module= sites, 3 templates) plus a semantic change (Module string -> element, throwing getter) and a reader wire-order contract. Branch is broadly red pre-existing, so regressions must be identified by failure-NAME diff vs a captured baseline, not counts.

actions.context: Stage A: ActionName->Name. Deleted the computed qualified Name FIRST so every qualified consumer surfaced as a compile error instead of silently flipping meaning. Per Ingi, ToString() is the object's own name; qualified form composed from both objects at use sites (overrides module-owns-action.md).
Dead templates: referenced nowhere live, and both read a.Parameters (plural) which does not exist so the block always rendered empty. Ingi confirmed deletion.

Stage B: action.Module is the module element (throwing getter). Reader resolves the wire name -> element, so an unknown module fails at READ (Ingi: the LLM should be told). Deleted the legacy module-name-separator repair. Schema partial's double string re-resolve collapsed.

Mint() published _actions=new() before filling it while _actions is the guard readers test -> concurrent reader saw an empty catalog. Fixed publish-order. Ingi then named the deeper defect: Mint itself is a hack; the registry owning each module's action map is the obpv.

Reverted the born-complete-in-ctor attempt (uncommitted; still fetched from the parent, and perturbed a shared-state race in scheme registration). Wrote up the real target: module owns its actions; registry owns modules only; Mint disappears rather than being fixed.

module-owns-its-actions ruling: registry index dissolves into modules (completion of module-owns-action); Q1 registry-local entry map not action.list (catalog must not carry Run/Output/Validate); Q2 one storage two filtered faces, role minted at registration; Q3 ActionEntry module-owned, dispose follows ownership; Q4 ToString overrule accepted + doc patched; born-complete kills the stamped catalog Context (Schema reaches App via Module navigation). Same release as module-owns-action core.
